content: Ibn Turka then treats the meaning of the Hour by the same seven levels, giving Q 54:1-2 as: the day of resurrection has drawn nigh and the moon is split, but unbelievers who see a sign say it is obvious sorcery. He explains the Hour as the day when all that has existed from pre-eternity to post-eternity is judged by its actions, weighed in the balance of true justice.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, R. Shaqq-i Qamar u Bayān-i Sāʿat
